Field notebook 'Doris Day 1 (structure)': structure notes on Kasira, P[ulau] Arguni, Sekar and Kaiwai (inside-cover index '1 Kasira / 5 p. arguni / 9 Sekar / 13 Kaiwai'). new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: quote-too-thin. Grace's one-line field summary '5 vowels, (length ?), stress [length prob. part of accent system]' records that stress is a relevant feature of Səkar (identity secure, first-hand 1955-56) but states no position or contrast; the given 'unclear' reading is right, the quote just carries no placement information (his pronoun stress marks are all penultimate). | checker: Opened the scan we hold (pp.7-8 viewed as images). p.7 is headed 'Səkar', notebook p.9: consonant chart b d (j) g / p t k / f s / m n (ŋ) / r,y,w and, right column, '5 vowels, (length ?), stress [length prob. part of accent system].' p.8: yai e- / o o- / 'ia i- / 'ita ita- / 'yami yami- / 'imi im…
new_statements.relation_note: Only first-hand prosodic remark on Sekar found anywhere: stress exists as a noted feature, length probably epiphenomenal to accent; position not stated. Also gives consonant inventory, 'No noun suffixes !', possessive prefixes e-/o-/i-/ita-/yami-/imi-/sina-, four verb subject-prefix patterns.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Grace records Sekar as having five vowels, doubtful vowel length, and STRESS as a feature of the sound system, adding that length is probably a by-product of the accent system. In his notebook convention the right-hand column lists the prosodic features he judged relevant/distinctive (he lists 'stress' for Sekar and Kaiwai but not for Kasira), so the note implies stress matters (possibly contrastive) in Sekar, but he states NO rule for its position. His own stress marks on the disyllabic free pronouns ('ia, 'ita, 'yami, 'imi, 'sina) are all word-initial = penultimate, consistent with the predominantly penultimate stress in the Donohue 2010 and de Vries 2004 stress-marked lists already tallied held by the project.
new_statements.exceptions: none; vowel length queried ('length ?') and attributed to the accent system
new_statements.identity_note: Headed 'Səkar' in Grace's hand; sits between his P. Arguni and Kaiwai notes from the same 1955-56 Fakfak-area fieldwork; his Swains Exercise Book 2 index places 'Səkar' (vocabulary p.121) with Kasira, Pulau Arguni, Tubiruasa (& Onin) under 'Fak2'; the pronoun set yai / o / 'ia / 'ita / 'yami / 'imi / 'sina matches Oninic (cf. Uruangnirin). This is the 'GG' Sekar source Blust 1993 cites. Not the unrelated seka1248.
